_source: Every field below was read out of the checkpoint itself with torch.load(map_location='cpu') and out of the faiss index with faiss.read_index, then confirmed by a real conversion. Nothing here is inferred from a filename. Script: questmod-research/verify_downloaded_rvc.py; output: rvc_logs/downloaded_check/.
_why_this_file: The quest's two scenes are spoken by exactly two actors: Mara (18 lines) and
V (11 lines). So the voice work needs a Mara model and a male V model, and a
Johnny model is for the ua-ua dub, not for this quest.
The overnight queue was 'mara v_male johnny' - 18 GPU hours - and two of those
three already existed on disk as downloaded models. This file records what they
actually are, so the question is never re-argued from filenames.

notes: tgt_sr = cpt['config'][-1]  - the INT in config, not the 'sr' key. That is why
MaleV's sr='48k' string is harmless: it is never read.
vocoder = cpt.get('vocoder','HiFi-GAN') - so a pre-Applio checkpoint with no
vocoder key gets HiFi-GAN, which is what those models were trained with.
embedder_model is NOT read from the checkpoint - it is an argument to the
inference call, default 'contentvec'. Both models want contentvec.

inference._why: 1.0 leaves the model's own output alone. The previous 0.0 was WRONG and actively harmful: change_rms rescales the output until its RMS matches the source, which made a railed generator produce a plausible level table. The old note here even recorded the symptom - 'at 1.0 this model emits -5.1 dBFS from a -21.6 dBFS source and is invariant to input level' - and read it as a property of the setting. An output invariant to its input level is a railed model. See D36.
inference._check_before_use: tools/rvc_check_model.py <model>  - exits non-zero if the model emits noise

_measured_2026_09_08.how: questmod-research/check_mara_g.py and check_mara.py - torch.load on CPU over the whole preserved 2026-09-06 series.
generator_never_learned: L2 norm of every float tensor falls monotonically 443.1926 (e10) -> 434.4345 (e200).
Monotone shrink with no growth anywhere is AdamW weight decay acting on a ZERO gradient.
(1 - lr*wd)**steps with lr=1e-4, wd=0.01, 26200 steps predicts ~2.6% shrink; measured 1.98%.
Per-decade max|delta| collapses to fp16-representable powers of two (7.812e-03 = 2**-7, 1.953e-03 = 2**-9).
From epoch 170 on, max|delta| is EXACTLY 0.0 - three consecutive decades of a bit-identical generator.
_measured_2026_09_08.discriminator_died: D_2333333.pth: 165/165 tensors non-finite, exp_avg_sq nan, GradScaler scale exactly 0.0 at 21287 steps.
root_cause: fp16 GradScaler collapse. The FORWARD pass emits a non-finite value; GradScaler can only respond
by halving the loss scale and skipping the step, which does not change the forward pass, so it
halves forever: 2**16 -> 2**-40 by epoch 10 -> 0.0. Long before zero, loss*scale underflows fp16's
smallest subnormal (6e-8), so backward yields bit-zero gradients that contain no inf - the scaler
is satisfied and the optimizer steps on zeros. At scale 0.0, unscale_ multiplies by 1/0 = inf and
0*inf = nan. Confirmed identically on johnny's preserved series (exp_avg_sq decayed at exactly
beta2**n, 3.53e-05 per 10 epochs against 3.5e-05 predicted, for nine consecutive decades).
_measured_2026_09_08.supersedes: _broken_how below, which blamed GPU contention (D34/D36). Contention was real but was not this. The same collapse reproduced on johnny with the card to itself.
_measured_2026_09_08.the_fix: precision fp32 in /mnt/sata/Applio/assets/config.json. NOT bf16: gfx1030/RDNA2 has no bf16 matrix instructions, so bf16 is emulated and was still inside MIOpen kernel JIT after 19 minutes without clearing step 0. train.py now raises if a whole epoch logs grad/norm == 0, so a repeat fails in minutes instead of 16 hours.
_measured_2026_09_08.cheap_proof_before_committing_a_night: Run 10 epochs at fp32 (~1.5 h) and check grad/norm_d and grad/norm_g in tensorboard are non-zero. With gradients actually flowing, a 626-clip fine-tune does not need 200 epochs - 60-80 is the usual range, ~10-13 h at fp32, i.e. one night rather than a couple of days.

_root_cause_found_2026_09_08.what: The fp16 collapse is a single line in rvc/train/losses.py, not a hardware or precision problem.
_root_cause_found_2026_09_08.why_it_overflows: logs_p is a log-variance, in practice -4 to -7, so exp(-2*logs_p) reaches exp(8)..exp(14) = 2.98e3..1.20e6. fp16's maximum is 65504. exp() returns inf, kl.sum() is inf, loss_gen_all is inf.
_root_cause_found_2026_09_08.why_gradscaler_could_not_save_it: An inf in the FORWARD pass is the one case GradScaler cannot handle. It responds by halving the loss scale and skipping the step - and halving the scale does not change a forward exp(). So it halved 2**16 down to exactly 0.0 over ~100 epochs while the generator learned nothing.
_root_cause_found_2026_09_08.why_it_was_not_obvious: kl_loss and feature_loss are called OUTSIDE the autocast block (train.py ~733). Inside autocast torch promotes exp() to fp32 automatically - it is on autocast's fp32 list precisely because it overflows. Moving those calls out of autocast looks like good hygiene and is what removed the protection. discriminator_loss and generator_loss in the same file DO call .float(); kl_loss and feature_loss did not.
_root_cause_found_2026_09_08.the_fix: losses.py: cast z_p/logs_q/m_p/logs_p/z_mask to .float() in kl_loss, and rl/gl to .float() in feature_loss. Backup at losses.py.bak-20260908.
_root_cause_found_2026_09_08.precision_verdict: fp16 is CORRECT for this card and is what assets/config.json is set to. The earlier fp32 and bf16 recommendations are both withdrawn: bf16 has no matrix instructions on gfx1030 and is emulated, and fp32 was only ever a way to dodge the overflow that is now fixed at source.
_root_cause_found_2026_09_08.SUPERSEDED: This entry named kl_loss as THE cause. It was necessary but not sufficient - see _root_cause_corrected_2026_09_08. Keeping it because the kl_loss fix is still correct and still applied.

_root_cause_corrected_2026_09_08.what: MIOpen's fp16 convolution backward-weights kernel returns NaN in the HiFi-GAN NSF vocoder.
_root_cause_corrected_2026_09_08.how_found: torch.autograd.set_detect_anomaly armed at step 60, where the GradScaler loss scale is ~0.03 and an overflow of the scaled gradient is arithmetically impossible. It reported: Function 'ConvolutionBackward0' returned nan values in its 1th output, forward call rvc/lib/algorithm/residuals.py:78 (x = conv2(x)), reached via synthesizers.py:191 self.dec(...) -> hifigan_nsf.py:202 resblock(x). Output 1 of ConvolutionBackward0 is grad_weight.
_root_cause_corrected_2026_09_08.why_the_kl_theory_was_wrong: kl_loss really did overflow fp16 in the forward pass and really did need the .float() casts that reference VITS has always had - after that fix every loss term stayed finite for a full epoch. But the gradients were still NaN. A NaN that survives a loss scale of 2.3e-10 cannot be an overflow of the scaled gradient; the accumulator that breaks is inside the conv kernel. enc_p.* topping the non-finite parameter list was misleading - those are simply the parameters furthest upstream, inheriting NaN from the decoder through the shared graph.

measured_fp16.norm_d: nan/inf steps 0-3, finite 4-34, then exactly 0.0 for 98 steps
measured_fp16.loss_scale: 32768 at step 0 -> 2.3e-10 by step 131, halving nearly every step

_root_cause_corrected_2026_09_08.also_verified: fp32->fp16 overflow on this GPU yields inf, not nan, including through ToCopyBackward0 - so the NaN is not a cast artefact.
_root_cause_corrected_2026_09_08.precision_verdict: fp32. Not a preference - fp16 produces NaN weight gradients in the vocoder on gfx1030 and cannot train this model. bf16 is untested since the earlier attempt only ever measured a cold MIOpen kernel compile.

_startup_fix_2026_09_08.cause: MIOpen namespaces its kernel cache by build hash. The build changed between Jun 15 and Sep 6, so the Sep 5-6 runs started completely cold and JIT-compiled the whole kernel set through comgr, single-threaded on CPU. There is no .kdb on this system for any architecture, so kernels are always compiled once then cached in the user ukdb.

inert_settings_removed.MIOPEN_CACHE_DIR: compile-time #ifdef (binary_cache.cpp:63), never read from the environment
inert_settings_removed.MIOPEN_CUSTOM_CACHE_DIR: replaces the WHOLE path including the version segment - pointing it at /mnt/ssd/miopen_cache aims MIOpen above the warm cache and silently starts an empty database. Do not set it.
inert_settings_removed.APPLIO_CUDNN_BENCHMARK: was inert because train.py's patch had been reverted to a hardcoded benchmark = True. Re-applied.

measured.note: 2.1x per step at identical precision - the gain is the find mode, not the dtype.

mara._history_2026_09_06_fp16_why_it_is_only_: The 200-epoch run took an amdgpu gfxhub page fault at 2026-09-04 11:30:44 (pid 1584013) after nine hours of sharing the GPU with an orphaned trainer from an earlier queue run. See D34. --save-every-epoch 10 had already written this checkpoint, and it is the same small inference checkpoint format as the final <model>.pth - not a resume state. The .index survived because core.py builds it from logs/mara/extracted/*.npy, independently of the weights.
mara._history_2026_09_06_fp16_open: 110/200. Re-queueing mara after johnny resumes from this checkpoint and costs only the remaining 90 epochs. Whether the extra 90 are audible is a listening decision, not a technical one.

_history_2026_09_06_fp16_broken_how.measured: 100% of samples at full scale at volume_envelope=1.0; the level in the source's silent frames is -0.1 dB where a healthy model gives -57 to -96 dB
_history_2026_09_06_fp16_broken_how.controls_pass: JohnnySilverhand_365e and MaleV-Cyberpunk2077 run clean through the identical pipeline, so the fault is this checkpoint, not the settings or the chain
_history_2026_09_06_fp16_broken_how.collapsed_between_epochs: 40 and 50, i.e. 08:01:27 - 08:29:54 on 2026-09-04, during the shared-GPU run of D34
_history_2026_09_06_fp16_broken_how.rot_started_earlier: energy above 8 kHz climbs 1.12 -> 2.59 -> 3.46% over epochs 20/30/40, so no early checkpoint is a safe base to resume from
_history_2026_09_06_fp16_broken_how.leading_cause: GPU contention - two orphaned trainers, an OOM and a page fault. Inferred, not proven: johnny trains healthily on the same fp16 default with the card to itself

mara._stale__verified_by: questmod-research/verify_mara_salvage.py - torch.load on CPU with all three visible-device vars blanked and `assert not torch.cuda.is_available()`, then two real conversions (in-domain and cross-voice). Log: rvc_logs/mara_salvage_check.log, audio: rvc_logs/mara_salvage_check/.
mara._why_that_date_matters: Read out of the checkpoint by torch.load, not off the filename or the mtime. A file named mara_200e_26200s.pth ALSO existed from the failed 2026-09-06 run, and Applio's save is `if not os.path.exists(m)` (rvc/train/train.py:1123) - it SKIPS rather than overwrites, so that collision would have silently discarded this save had the old file not been renamed first. The embedded date is the only field that cannot be faked by a copy.
mara._epoch_choice: 120 holds the loss minimum (13.837, never beaten in the 80 epochs after it) and the best noise floor (SNR 29.4 vs 28.3). 200 is what the user listened to and approved. Every pair from epoch 090 to 200 differs by <=1 dB of band shape, which is at or under JND, so this was a coin toss and the ear settled it. Do not swap checkpoints for the 0.55 dB.

male_v.checkpoint_format: pre-Applio RVC: keys are config/f0/info/sr/version only

But the TTS half is no longer UNVERIFIED: questmod-research/verify_tts_chain.sh ran edge-tts 7.2.8 -> ffmpeg 48k mono -> RVC/mara on CPU (volume_envelope 0.0) -> tools/wav_to_wem.py -> vgmstream, and the container round trip returns sample-identical int16.
